meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: What day of the week is it today?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken contraction of 이것.
Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.
Often paired with 나다 (실감이 나다) to mean something finally feels real.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

meanings.note: Contrasted with 신용카드 (credit card).

examples.trans: There is no cash in my wallet.

meanings.note: Primary everyday meaning.
Used at a bank or ATM for taking out cash.

examples.trans: I withdrew money at the bank.
I am looking for my keys.

meanings.note: Polite, respectful word for mother (compared to 엄마, mom).
Placed before the verb it modifies.
Humble counterpart of 주다, used when giving to elders or superiors.

examples.trans: I gave a present to my grandmother.
May I ask you a question?

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g. 우세요, 웁니다).

examples.trans: I cried because the movie was sad.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I couldn't contact you because I was busy.

meanings.note: Used when explaining why something happened.

examples.trans: What is the reason you are late?

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Spoken contraction of bound noun 것; used in -(으)ㄴ/는 거예요 to ask or explain a situation.

examples.trans: Where are you going right now?

meanings.note: Exclamation of realization, surprise, or hesitation.
Standard polite negative reply.
Humble first-person pronoun used in polite speech; becomes 제가 before subject marker 가.

meanings.en: to like, to be fond of
meanings.note: Takes an object marked with 을/를.

examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?

meanings.note: Honorific noun and counter for people, used instead of 사람.

examples.trans: That person over there is our teacher.
How many people are in your party?

meanings.note: Division of a television network that produces variety and entertainment shows.

examples.trans: He works in the variety department at a broadcasting station.
Variety department PDs are always busy.

meanings.note: Honorific counterpart of 있다 (to be in a place).

examples.trans: Is the director in the office right now?

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.

meanings.note: Derived from 가깝다 (to be close).

examples.trans: There is a park close to my house.

meanings.note: Auxiliary adjective attached to a verb stem with -고 (-고 싶다).

examples.trans: I want to go to Korea.
I want to drink a cup of coffee.

meanings.en: older sister; older female friend or senior
meanings.note: Used by a younger male speaker.

examples.trans: Nuna, do you have time today?

meanings.note: A person who gathers and reports news.

examples.trans: My dream is to become a reporter.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.

meanings.note: Korean says 시험을 보다 ('see an exam') for taking a test.

examples.trans: I am taking a Korean exam tomorrow.
Did you prepare well for the exam?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.
Action of coming together with someone.
